rounds.text: Impera Worldwide Ltd exhibits fundamental financial instability characterized by persistent value destruction and poor capital efficiency. The company reports a deeply negative return on equity of -112.0% [E12] and a median ROE over the last three years of -61% [E19], which is flagged as a significant negative [E35]. This is compounded by an operating margin of -127% [E21] and negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -0.08 Cr [E25, E26]. The valuation is disconnected from these poor fundamentals, as evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of 994.03x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.17x [E6]. Furthermore, the company faces operational risks including high debtors of 438 days [E36] and a low interest coverage ratio [E34]. Conceded: the company has shown recent profit growth of 46% [E15] and a 40% share price increase over the last year [E17]. Despite these recent metrics, the long-term compounded profit growth remains stagnant at 0% over three years [E14], suggesting that the current financial performance lacks the consistency required to justify its premium valuation.
